note: Adapted from the original English description of Scheffrahn & Křeček 1999, where the species was established as Cryptotermes cryptognathus n. sp.; type locality Booby South Point, Jamaica (the original also cites Scheffrahn et al. 1998: 239). Alates: 4 females and 6 males from 2 colonies; soldiers: 18 individuals from 6 colonies. The original stresses that this species resembles no other species of the genus worldwide, because its extremely small mandibles are completely hidden beneath the postclypeus and the frontal face when closed; in half of the individuals the mandibles are not visible at all in dorsal view, and in the rest only one tip protrudes. The rows for left mandible length and total body length were not printed with the table in the photocopy and are therefore not cited here.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body pale yellow, the abdominal tergites yellow. Head pale yellow, with a slightly darker transverse band between the compound eyes. Chevron on the forewing scale faint, concolorous with the yellow of the posterior corners of the pronotum; rest of the pronotum pale yellow, with a distinct white median line crossing the white transverse band to form a cross. Labrum, antennae and legs yellow, only the femora pale yellow. Wing membrane almost transparent, with a pale golden iridescence; anterior sclerotized veins pale orange, fading towards the apex. Cranial sutures indistinct. Compound eyes medium-sized, oval. Ocelli oval, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 13—16-segmented, usually 14 or 15, the segment formula variable. Pronotum distinctly narrower than the head across the compound eyes; nearly square, the sides nearly straight and slightly divergent posteriorly, or slightly convex; anterior margin moderately concave, the posterior margin shallowly concave in the middle. Radius of the forewing meeting the wing margin at one third to one half of the wing length from the suture; radial sector with 4 branches. Arolium present.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Measurements (4 females and 6 males, 2 colonies, in mm, the morphotype in parentheses): head length including the labrum 1.05—1.16 (1.10±0.037, 1.13); head length to the postclypeus 0.80—0.85 (0.83±0.014, 0.83); maximum head width across the compound eyes 0.87—0.90 (0.88±0.013, 0.90); compound eye diameter 0.28—0.31 (0.29±0.0060, 0.30); shortest distance from the compound eye to the posterior margin of the head 0.11—0.15 (0.13±0.011, 0.12); ocellus diameter 0.10—0.11 (0.11±0.006, 0.11); maximum pronotal length 0.54—0.59 (0.56±0.019, 0.57); maximum pronotal width 0.74—0.80 (0.77±0.026, 0.78); total body length with wings 7.67—8.66 (8.16±0.32, 8.52); total body length without wings 3.69—4.26 (3.95±0.23, 4.26); forewing length (from the suture) 6.25—6.96 (6.60±0.21, 6.82); maximum forewing width 1.58—1.78 (1.66±0.064, 1.75).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head, in dorsal view, almost black from the anterior third to half, becoming rusty to chestnut brown behind; in lateral view almost black from the anterior third to half, the posterior part rusty or chestnut brown, with a very narrow orange-yellow band along the foramen magnum. Mandibles varying from rusty orange to chestnut brown, the darker individuals with an iridescence. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a rusty orange bow-shaped patch, the remainder pale yellow. Head, in dorsal view, oval, only the antennae and palps exposed; the sides nearly parallel, slightly convergent anteriorly, with a shallow constriction in the middle; the anterior and posterior corners rounded. Head surface mostly smooth and shining (including the frontal face and the frontal margin), with fine, elongate, shallow rugae only on the posterior quarter and the sides. Frontal margin stout in both dorsal and frontal view, its width in the middle twice its width at the sides; the anterior edge almost straight in the middle, then projecting forward on either side; the frontal margin slightly raised above the vertex, forming a distinct arc in lateral view. Frontal face distinctly convex in the middle, with a shallow depression on each side; the convexity continuous downwards with the postclypeus, narrowing upwards to a point and separated from the frontal margin. Frontal face meeting the vertex face at 70°. Labrum very short, broadly rounded. Frontal horns very short but broad, almost continuous with the frontal margin. Genal horns minute. Mandibles extremely short; in dorsal view completely concealed by the postclypeus and the frontal face in half of the individuals, in frontal view often invisible except for the bent base, the rest covered by the labrum; in other individuals one tip is visible. Mandible base raised and bent, distinctly turned downwards in lateral view; the first marginal tooth of each mandible short but distinct. Compound eyes oval, small, or larger and slightly pigmented in soldier—nymph intermediates. Antennae 10—14-segmented, usually 11 or 12, the segment formula variable. Pronotum broadly shield-shaped, the anterior margin shallowly incised, the posterior margin almost straight, the sides slightly convex; the anterior corners bent at almost a right angle. Anterior margin of the pronotum densely covered with blunt undulations.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements (18 individuals, 6 colonies, in mm, holotype): head length to the tip of the mandibles 1.12—1.24 (1.19±0.031, 1.18); head length to the frontal horns 1.10—1.28 (1.20±0.037, 1.20); frontal margin width 0.90—0.96 (0.94±0.023, 0.96); outer span of the frontal horns 0.69—0.75 (0.71±0.022, 0.72); maximum head width 1.06—1.14 (1.09±0.022, 1.11); head height without the postmentum 0.70—0.83 (0.78±0.035, 0.82); maximum pronotal width 0.97—1.06 (1.02±0.027, 0.97); maximum pronotal length 0.62—0.75 (0.70±0.029, 0.67).
